correctness.rationale: The Weyl basis gives singular values sqrt(N)|A_g| with all normalization factors accounted for. Missing cyclic differences remove entire N-frequency rows. At N=q^2+q+1 full rank with support <=q+1 forces a Singer perfect difference set. A self-contained finite-field trace construction proves Singer existence for all prime powers. The exact difference character-sum identity gives three singular levels, AM-GM bounds the minimum coefficient globally with equality only for flat amplitudes, and a deleted Singer point maximizes rank for support <=q. Direct independent numerical lifting SVD and exact combinatorial counts are supplementary checks.

value.rationale: The object is the full operator tomography map under a natural hard constraint on window localization; optimal support and best achievable conditioning are concrete design invariants. The theorem determines minimal support, sharp worst-direction stability and all equalizers, a complete singular spectrum, and the minimal rank loss when the support budget is one atom smaller. This is a sharp complete sampling classification, not a fixed tiny-table recomputation. The scope is explicitly linear matrix recovery, not a claim about all nonlinear phase-retrieval settings.
